From kaninerecords.com:

"When you think of Palm Beach, Florida, what comes to mind? Palm trees swaying gently in the balmy breeze? Scantily-clad bikini buxom babes rollerblading down an infinite slab of coral-colored concrete? How about anthemic, bombastic, life-affirming indie pop? If the latter didn’t occur to you, let us introduce you to Surfer Blood: they call West Palm Beach home and, while still in their early 20s, have penned an album worth of catchy indie songs that even the most hook-laden power pop band would rightfully be jealous of.

Comprised of members JP (dubbed “The Mastermind” by the rest of the band), TJ, Thomas Brian and Marcos, Surfer Blood met one fateful night at an after party for Miami’s Ultra Festival, though they didn’t attend the festival itself (“We do not like the D’n’B,” they proclaim). After discussing music, what else, for the remainder of the night, JP decided to recruit the three other guys to perfect a couple of songs he had been working on for some time, and thus, the band was formed.

If you’re wondering about the name, the band ain’t got no surfer blood in them, and actually denounce the surfer kids of their youth for making their high school experience miserable. As for the moniker itself, one of the band members just randomly yelled it out over the radio in the backseat of the band’s car, which is as good a naming process as any.

In January 2010, Surfer Blood will release Astro Coast, their debut album, on Kanine Records. Their first single release, “Swim (To Reach the End)”, with its deliciously deafening swaths of reverb and feedback, comes across like early Orange Juice covering every song on Weezer’s Blue Album at once. When the whole nation is revving up the nostalgia for the blissed-out indie vibes of the early-to-mid-‘90s, expect Astro Coast to snag some serious fans as soon as it’s released."

data.description:
Come celebrate the holidays at The I Drive's first annual "Not Another Christmas Show" with very special guests RC Static, Chances Are High and Spontaneo!

This will be The I Drive's first Pittsburgh headliner, so be sure to come out and help make the holidays extra special for them!

For tickets, contact The I Drive on myspace or on here. Tickets are $8.00 advance and $10.00 day of show. We will even deliver!

-------------------------------

About The I Drive:

Picture a rock band that looks like they came straight out of a scene from “Detroit Rock City” or “Dazed And Confused” and play melodic rock songs with infectious hooks that leave you singing along in your head for days. Meet “The I Drive”, a four piece rock group from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania which originally formed in North Carolina in 2007 under the name The International Drive. Later that year, The International Drive released their debut EP “Finish What You Started” on Disco Technology Records with worldwide distribution. Shortly after the release of the band’s debut album, their record label folded leaving the band to again start from scratch. Their hard work and dedication landed them a spot in Alternative Press and on the front page of Purevolume.com.

After a relentless touring schedule promoting the EP, including shows supporting, Boys Like Girls, Armor For Sleep, and Four Year Strong, their single “So Call It Off” caught the ears of producers Matthew Gerrard (Kelly Clarkson, Jessica Simpson, Hannah Montana) and Robbie Nevil (Smash Mouth, High School Musical, Destiny’s Child) who then invited the band to join them at their Los Angeles recording studio, Track Record Recording Studios (The Offspring, Aerosmith, Pink, Goo Goo Dolls) to record their yet to be released follow-up.

-------------------------------

On Thursday, February 4th, 2010—the “radical reinvention” marketing and live event company—Monster Nature, is launching the “Healing Haiti Relief Show” to raise support funds for the victims of the recent earthquake in Haiti. Local downtown venue, Back Booth—located at 37 W. Pine St, off Orange Ave—has agreed to host the event with no overhead charge. Jesse Rosoff, co-founder of Monster Nature said, “The $5 suggested donation cover charge will directly benefit our selected charities, Doctors Without Borders, Mercy Corps, and Yele Haiti.”

The three chosen organizations are currently leaders in supplying relief to the Haiti earthquake crisis. “We chose Doctors Without Borders, Mercy Corps and Yele Haiti because they are organizations with low overhead through which a vast majority of donated money will have direct impact in the crisis zone,” says Monster Nature co-founder, Kyle J. Britt.

Monster Nature was founded on principals of charity and community, and has organized similar fundraising efforts in the past. The most recent music benefit Monster Nature hosted was last year, for Invisible Children, at Dungeon Lounge, in which the venue was sold-out:
http://205.209.52.72/x-1075-Orlando-Music-Examiner~y2009m10d7-Monster-Nature-Roars-onto-the-Scene

“Several talented Central Florida-based regional artists will be featured, each donating their normal performance fee to the cause,” explains Monster Nature Talent Director Sarah Conness. Live updates, show roster, and other details can be viewed at MonsterNature.com as they are announced. If anyone is interested in helping through sponsorship or other in-kind donations, they are invited to email healhaiti@monsternature.com.

Monster Nature can be reached by contacting Matthew Deicke, Public Relations Director at matthew@monsternature.com. 

Other Sources:
Doctors Without Borders - http://doctorswithoutborders.org/
Mercy Corps - http://www.mercycorps.org/
Yele Haiti - http://yele.org/
